sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered how Java handles numbers that don't quite fit? Let's explore type casting - your tool to convert between data types!

• What type casting is and why it matters
• How to widen and narrow data types
• Common pitfalls and how to avoid them

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you're pouring liquids between containers:
- A small cup (int) can easily fit into a large pitcher (double) - that's widening!
- But pouring a pitcher into a cup? You might spill some - that's narrowing, and you need to be careful!

Type casting works the same way with numbers in Java:
• **Widening**: Safe, automatic conversion (e.g., int → double)
  - Java does this for you behind the scenes
  - No data loss occurs

• **Narrowing**: Risky, manual conversion (e.g., double → int)
  - You must explicitly tell Java to do this
  - Can lose data (like decimal places)

sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how Type Casting works:

steps.title: Widening (Automatic)
steps.description: Java automatically converts smaller types to larger ones when needed.

steps.title: Narrowing (Manual)

steps.title: Mixed Operations
steps.description: Java automatically widens in mixed-type operations.

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Narrowing = risky (double → int), needs explicit cast
✓ Mixed operations automatically widen the smaller type

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use widening when possible - it's safer
Always check for data loss when narrowing
Remember: casting doesn't change the original variable
donts: Forget the cast when narrowing - causes errors!
Assume all conversions are safe (e.g., long → int)
Mix types without understanding the conversion
sections.protip: When in doubt, print the result to check for unexpected truncation!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Type Casting used in real apps?

examples.how: Converting precise double values to cents (int) for transactions
Converting floating-point coordinates to pixel positions (int)
Converting between different numeric formats when reading files

problem.description: Write a program that calculates the average of three test scores (as doubles) but displays the result as an integer percentage. Watch out for truncation!
hints: First calculate the average as a double
Then cast to int for the percentage
problem.explanation: We calculate the precise average first, then cast to int to get the whole number percentage. The decimal part is truncated (not rounded).

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Type casting converts between data types
📌 Widening = safe & automatic; Narrowing = risky & manual
📌 Practice casting with different numeric types
📌 Ready to handle user input next!
